q: (Only Allaah knows the correct meaning of these letters.)
v.s: Alif, Lām, Meem.
v.c: Alif-Lãm-Mĩm.

q: (the people of the Ahlul Kitaab who controlled the Byzantine Empire)
v.s: The Byzantines have been defeated
v.c: The Romans have been defeated

v.s: In the nearest land. But they, after their defeat, will overcome
v.c: in a nearby land. Yet following their defeat, they will triumph

q: years. All affairs are in Allaah's control from before
(it was therefore by Allaah's command that Persia won at first and that Rome won thereafter).
v.s: Within three to nine years. To God belongs the command [i.e., decree] before and after. And that day the believers will rejoice
v.c: within three to nine years. The ˹whole˺ matter rests with Allah before and after ˹victory˺. And on that day the believers will rejoice

q: (because like the Mu'mineen, the Ahlul Kitaab were also monotheists, whereas the Persians were polytheists).
(and will certainly assist the Muslims against the Mushrikeen),
v.s: In the victory of God. He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
v.c: at the victory willed by Allah. He gives victory to whoever He wills. For He is the Almighty, Most Merciful.

q: (to assist His Ambiyaa and those with them).
v.s: [It is] the promise of God. God does not fail in His promise, but most of the people do not know.
v.c: ˹This is˺ the promise of Allah. ˹And˺ Allah never fails in His promise. But most people do not know.

q: the life of this world whereas they are negligent
(do not want to understand the benefits)
(as a result, they will be unsuccessful in the Aakhirah).
v.s: They know what is apparent of the worldly life, but they, of the Hereafter, are unaware.
v.c: They ˹only˺ know the worldly affairs of this life, but are ˹totally˺ oblivious to the Hereafter.

q: (thought about the many signs of Allaah's power and Oneness)? (Have they not realised that)
Allaah has created the heavens and the earth with the truth

(Have they not reasoned that just as everything else in this world comes to an end, so too will the universe come to an end on the Day of Qiyaamah, when everyone will be required to face Allaah?) (However,)
(even though their very logic demands that a time must come when wrong-doers have to be taken to task and good-doers have to be rewarded).
v.s: Do they not contemplate within themselves? God has not created the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth and for a specified term. And indeed, many of the people, in [the matter of] the meeting with their Lord, are disbelievers.
v.c: Have they not reflected upon their own being? Allah only created the heavens and the earth and everything in between for a purpose and an appointed term. Yet most people are truly in denial of the meeting with their Lord!

q: not travelled in the lands and seen what was the plight
before them? Those people were mightier than them
ploughed the earth and developed it
(yet despite all of this, they were destroyed).
(with the message of Towheed, but they rejected the message).
It was not Allaah Who wronged them, but they wronged themselves
(by become of their inability to accept the truth when they committed kufr and rejected the Ambiyaa ﵊ hey were therefore responsible for the resultant punishment).
v.s: Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in power, and they plowed [or excavated] the earth and built it up more than they [i.e., the Makkans] have built it up, and their messengers came to them with clear evidences. And God would not ever have wronged them, but they were wronging themselves.
v.c: Have they not travelled throughout the land to see what was the end of those ˹destroyed˺ before them? They were far superior in might; they cultivated the land and developed it more than these ˹Meccans˺ ever have. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs. Allah would have never wronged them, but it was they who wronged themselves.

q: of those who perpetrated evil was evil
indeed because they rejected Allaah's Aayaat
v.s: Then the end of those who did evil was the worst [consequence] because they denied the signs of God and used to ridicule them.
v.c: Then most evil was the end of the evildoers for denying and mocking the signs of Allah.

q: Allaah originated creation and will repeat
(the act of creation on the Day of Qiyaamah when the dead will be brought back to life),
after which you will all be returned to Him
(to account for your actions in the world).
v.s: God begins creation; then He will repeat it; then to Him you will be returned.
v.c: It is Allah Who originates the creation, and will resurrect it. And then to Him you will ˹all˺ be returned.

q: The day when Qiyaamah will dawn, the criminals
(of escaping punishment because their guilt will be proven beyond doubt).
v.s: And the Day the Hour appears the criminals will be in despair.
v.c: On the Day the Hour will arrive, the wicked will be dumbstruck.

q: (their gods whom they ascribed as partners to Allaah)
v.s: And there will not be for them among their [alleged] partners any intercessors, and they will [then] be disbelievers in their partners.
v.c: There will be no intercessors for them from among their associate-gods, and they will ˹totally˺ deny their associate-gods.

q: On the day when Qiyaamah will take place, they
(and a person will fall either among the ranks of the Mu'mineen or the Kuffaar).
v.s: And the Day the Hour appears - that Day they will become separated.
v.c: And on the Day the Hour will arrive, the people will then be split ˹into two groups˺.

q: As for those who have Imaan and perform good deeds, they will be rejoicing in a garden
v.s: And as for those who had believed and done righteous deeds, they will be in a garden [of Paradise], delighted.
v.c: As for those who believed and did good, they will be rejoicing in a Garden.

q: As for those who commit kufr and who reject Our Aayaat and the meeting of the Aakhirah, these people will be exposed to punishment.
v.s: But as for those who disbelieved and denied Our verses and the meeting of the Hereafter, those will be brought into the punishment [to remain].
v.c: And as for those who disbelieved, and denied Our signs and the meeting ˹with Allah˺ in the Hereafter, they will be confined in punishment.

q: (during the Maghrib salaah and Isha salaah)
v.s: So exalted is God when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning.
v.c: So glorify Allah in the evening and in the morning—

q: All praise in the heavens and the earth belong to Him, and
(in addition to glorifying His purity during the mornings and evenings, you should also)
glorify His purity during the latter part of the day
v.s: And to Him is [due all] praise throughout the heavens and the earth. And [exalted is He] at night and when you are at noon.
v.c: all praise is for Him in the heavens and the earth—as well as in the afternoon, and at noon.

q: brings forth the living from the dead
(such as a chicken from an egg or a Mu'min from a Kaafir),
(such as an egg from a hen or a Kaafir from a Mu'min)
and revives the earth after its death
(by causing vegetation to flourish on ground that was previously barren).
(as Allaah causes the dead earth to be revived)
will you be brought back to life
(on the Day of Qiyaamah after your death).
v.s: He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living and brings to life the earth after its lifelessness. And thus will you be brought out.
v.c: He brings forth the living from the dead and the dead from the living. And He gives life to the earth after its death. And so will you be brought forth ˹from the grave˺.
v.h: Allah’s Power over Life and Death

q: (that demonstrate His power and prove His Oneness)
is that He has created you
v.s: And of His signs is that He created you from dust; then, suddenly you were human beings dispersing [throughout the earth].
v.c: One of His signs is that He created you from dust, then—behold!—you are human beings spreading over ˹the earth˺.

q: Also among His Aayaat is that He has created spouses for you from yourselves
so that you may find solace
with her and He has placed
(most clearly seen during youth and adulthood)
(blessed you with a great deal of)
between you. There are certainly Aayaat in this for people who contemplate
v.s: And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you may find tranquillity in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
v.c: And one of His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves so that you may find comfort in them. And He has placed between you compassion and mercy. Surely in this are signs for people who reflect.

q: Also among His Aayaat is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the variety of your languages and colours
(of your skin despite the fact that you all came from Aadam and Hawwa).
There are certainly Aayaat in this for those who have knowledge
v.s: And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the diversity of your languages and your colors. Indeed in that are signs for those of knowledge.
v.c: And one of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the diversity of your languages and colours. Surely in this are signs for those of ˹sound˺ knowledge.

q: Also among His Aayaat is your sleep by night and by day
(when you are oblivious of everything and wake up refreshed),
and your seeking from His bounty
There are certainly Aayaat in this for those who listen
v.s: And of His signs is your sleep by night and day and your seeking of His bounty. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen.
v.c: And one of His signs is your sleep by night and by day ˹for rest˺ as well as your seeking His bounty ˹in both˺. Surely in this are signs for people who listen.

q: Also among His Aayaat is that He shows you lightning which aroused
He sends rain from the sky, thereby reviving the earth after its death. There are certainly Aayaat in this for people who understand
v.s: And of His signs is [that] He shows you the lightening [causing] fear and aspiration, and He sends down rain from the sky by which He brings to life the earth after its lifelessness. Indeed in that are signs for a people who use reason.
v.c: And one of His signs is that He shows you lightning, inspiring ˹you with˺ hope and fear. And He sends down rain from the sky, reviving the earth after its death. Surely in this are signs for people who understand.

q: Also among His Aayaat is that the sky and the earth stand
when He will call for you from the earth
(from your graves to account to Allaah for all you did and believed).
v.s: And of His signs is that the heaven and earth stand [i.e., remain] by His command. Then when He calls you with a [single] call from the earth, immediately you will come forth.
v.c: And one of His signs is that the heavens and the earth persist by His command. Then when He calls you out of the earth just once, you will instantly come forth.

q: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Everything is subservient
v.s: And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and earth. All are to Him devoutly obedient.
v.c: And to Him belong all those in the heavens and the earth—all are subject to His Will.

q: (because it will be easier to do something the second time).
His is the Highest glory in the heavens and the earth
(because Only He deserves to be worshipped),
and He is the Mighty, the Wise.
v.s: And it is He who begins creation; then He repeats it, and that is [even] easier for Him. To Him belongs the highest description [i.e., attribute] in the heavens and earth. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
v.c: And He is the One Who originates the creation then will resurrect it—which is even easier for Him. To Him belong the finest attributes in the heavens and the earth. And He is the Almighty, All-Wise.

q: (For you to understand the foolishness of Shirk,)
Allaah gives you an example relating to your own selves
which We have given you, making you all
(when you wish to spend from the wealth)
Thus do We explain Aayaat for people of understanding.

(Allaah asks the Mushrikeen if they would be pleased with the idea of seeking permission from their slaves to spend their own wealth, as they would have to do if their slaves were to be their partners. When man dislikes having partners, who are human like himself in jointly owning property, how can he expect Allaah to tolerate the behaviour of Mushrikeen, who ascribe such partners to Him, who are incomparably inferior to Him?)
v.s: He presents to you an example from yourselves. Do you have among those whom your right hands possess [i.e., slaves] any partners in what We have provided for you so that you are equal therein [and] would fear them as your fear of one another [within a partnership]? Thus do We detail the verses for a people who use reason.
v.c: He sets forth for you an example ˹drawn˺ from your own lives: would you allow some of those ˹bondspeople˺ in your possession to be your equal partners in whatever ˹wealth˺ We have provided you, keeping them in mind as you are mindful of your peers? This is how We make the signs clear for people who understand.

q: Who can guide the one whom Allaah has sent astray? They will have no helpers
v.s: But those who wrong follow their [own] desires without knowledge. Then who can guide one whom God has sent astray? And for them there are no helpers.
v.c: In fact, the wrongdoers merely follow their desires with no knowledge. Who then can guide those Allah has left to stray? They will have no helpers.

q: So focus your attention only on this Deen as a Haneef
(one who turns away from every other religion). (Accept and follow)
(the built-in inherent capacity every human has to accept Islaam)
on which He created mankind. There can be no change to Allaah's creation
Deen, but most people do not know
(and therefore remain Kuffaar because they refuse to utilise this capacity to accept the truth).
v.s: So direct your face [i.e., self] toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fitrah of God upon which He has created [all] people. No change should there be in the creation of God. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.
v.c: So be steadfast in faith in all uprightness ˹O Prophet˺—the natural Way of Allah which He has instilled in ˹all˺ people. Let there be no change in this creation of Allah. That is the Straight Way, but most people do not know.

q: turning solely to Allaah, fear Him, establish salaah and do not be from the Mushrikeen...
v.s: [Adhere to it], turning in repentance to Him, and fear Him and establish prayer and do not be of those who associate others with God
v.c: ˹O believers!˺ Always turn to Him ˹in repentance˺, be mindful of Him, and establish prayers. And do not be polytheists—

q: from those who divided their religion and have been split into many factions, each faction
(and thereby refusing to accept the truth).
v.s: [Or] of those who have divided their religion and become sects, every faction rejoicing in what it has.
v.c: ˹like˺ those who have divided their faith and split into sects, each rejoicing in what they have.

q: people, they call to their Rabb, turning only to Him
(without bothering to pray to their gods).
Then, when He allows them the taste of His mercy
suddenly a group of them ascribe partners to their Rabb...
v.s: And when adversity touches the people, they call upon their Lord, turning in repentance to Him. Then when He lets them taste mercy from Him, at once a party of them associate others with their Lord,
v.c: When people are touched with hardship, they cry out to their Lord, turning to Him ˹alone˺. But as soon as He gives them a taste of His mercy, a group of them associates ˹others˺ with their Lord ˹in worship˺,

q: (Instead of worshipping Allaah out of gratitude to Him, they worship others who have done nothing for them.)
(in this world by doing as you please)!
Soon you will come to know
(the error of your ways when Allaah's punishment strikes you).
v.s: So that they will deny what We have granted them. Then enjoy yourselves, for you are going to know.
v.c: becoming ungrateful for whatever ˹favours˺ We have given them. So enjoy yourselves, for soon you will know.

q: to them, which speaks about what
they ascribe as partners to Allaah?
v.s: Or have We sent down to them an authority [i.e., a proof or scripture], and it speaks of what they were associating with Him?
v.c: Or have We sent down to them an authority which attests to what they associate ˹with Him˺?

q: When We allow people to taste Our mercy
about it. However, when any difficulty
afflicts them because of the sins they commit, they suddenly lose hope
(of ever recovering from the difficulty, thereby indicating that they have no faith and do no rely on Allaah).
v.s: And when We let the people taste mercy, they rejoice therein, but if evil afflicts them for what their hands have put forth, immediately they despair.
v.c: If We give people a taste of mercy, they become prideful ˹because˺ of it. But if they are afflicted with an evil for what their hands have done, they instantly fall into despair.

q: Do they not see that Allaah increases sustenance for whoever He wills and decreases
There are certainly Aayaat in this for those who have Imaan.
v.s: Do they not see that God extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
v.c: Have they not seen that Allah gives abundant or limited provisions to whoever He wills? Surely in this are signs for people who believe.

q: So give the relative his right
(behave kindly toward him and assist him wherever possible),
as well as the poor and the traveller
(all of whom should be assisted in every possible manner).
This is best for those who seek Allaah's pleasure
(because assisting Allaah's creation pleases Allaah greatly).
(people who fulfil the rights of others)
v.s: So give the relative his right, as well as the needy and the traveler. That is best for those who desire the countenance of God, and it is they who will be the successful.
v.c: So give your close relatives their due, as well as the poor and the ˹needy˺ traveller. That is best for those who seek the pleasure of Allah, and it is they who will be successful.

q: you pay to increase people's wealth does not increase in Allaah's sight
(because interest destroys the blessings of one's wealth even though the wealth seems to be increasing in value). (On the other hand)
Whatever you pay as zakaah, seeking Allaah's pleasure, such people
(their rewards, even though their wealth seems to be decreasing in value).
v.s: And whatever you give for interest [i.e., advantage] to increase within the wealth of people will not increase with God. But what you give in zakāh, desiring the countenance of God - those are the multipliers.
v.c: Whatever loans you give, ˹only˺ seeking interest at the expense of people’s wealth will not increase with Allah. But whatever charity you give, ˹only˺ seeking the pleasure of Allah—it is they whose reward will be multiplied.

m: He will cause you to die
q: It is Allaah Who has created you, then sustains you, will then give you death and again give you life
Are there any of your partners
who can do any of this? Allaah is Pure
and Exalted above the partners they
(because none can do what He can do).
v.s: God is the one who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, and then will give you life. Are there any of your "partners" who does anything of that? Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
v.c: It is Allah Who created you, then gives you provisions, then will cause you to die, and then will bring you back to life. Can any of your associate-gods do any of this? Glorified and Exalted is He above what they associate with Him ˹in worship˺!

m: so that He may let them taste
q: on land and at sea because of the
actions of man and so that Allaah may let them taste
v.s: Corruption has appeared throughout the land and sea by [reason of] what the hands of people have earned so He [i.e., God] may let them taste part of [the consequence of] what they have done that perhaps they will return [to righteousness].
v.c: Corruption has spread on land and sea as a result of what people’s hands have done, so that Allah may cause them to taste ˹the consequences of˺ some of their deeds and perhaps they might return ˹to the Right Path˺.

q: Say, “Travel in the lands and see what was the plight
(you. See how Allaah's punishment destroyed them and learn a lesson from this).
(those who were punished in the past)
v.s: Say, [O Muhammad], “Travel through the land and observe how was the end of those before. Most of them were associators [of others with God].
v.c: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Travel throughout the land and see what was the end of those ˹destroyed˺ before ˹you˺—most of them were polytheists.”

q: So focus your attention on the upright Deen
comes when there will be no defence against
Allaah. On that day people will be
(into two groups; one destined for Jannah and the other for Jahannam).
v.s: So direct your face [i.e., self] toward the correct religion before a Day comes from God of which there is no repelling. That Day, they will be divided.
v.c: So be steadfast in the Upright Faith ˹O Prophet˺, before the coming of a Day from Allah that cannot be averted. On that Day the people will be divided:

q: Whoever commits kufr, his kufr will be to his detriment
(because he will suffer eternal punishment for it). (On the other hand,)
carries out a good deed, such people will be preparing the ground
v.s: Whoever disbelieves - upon him is [the consequence of] his disbelief. And whoever does righteousness - they are for themselves preparing,
v.c: those who disbelieved will bear ˹the burden of˺ their own disbelief; and those who did good will have prepared for themselves ˹eternal homes˺,

q: ...so that Allaah may reward from His grace
those who have Imaan and who do good deeds. Without doubt, Allaah does not like the Kaafiroon.
v.s: That He may reward those who have believed and done righteous deeds out of His bounty. Indeed, He does not like the disbelievers.
v.c: so that He may ˹generously˺ reward those who believe and do good, out of His grace. He truly does not like the disbelievers.

q: Among His Aayaat is that He sends the winds as carriers of good news
(indicating to man that rain is soon to arrive. The wind is sent)
let people have a taste His mercy
to allow ships to sail by His command so that you seek from His bounty
and so that you may show gratitude
v.s: And of His signs is that He sends the winds as bringers of good tidings and to let you taste His mercy [i.e., rain] and so the ships may sail at His command and so you may seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful.
v.c: And one of His signs is that He sends the winds, ushering in good news ˹of rain˺ so that He may give you a taste of His mercy, and that ships may sail by His command, and that you may seek His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful.

q: We have undoubtedly sent many Rusul before you to their nations, who brought clear signs
(to prove that they were true messengers of Allaah). (However, despite this, the people rejected the message of Towheed that the Ambiyaa ﵊ brought and harassed the Mu'mineen. Therefore)
We then exacted revenge from those who sinned
(by already punishing them in this world)
It has always been Our bounden responsibility to
v.s: And We have already sent messengers before you to their peoples, and they came to them with clear evidences; then We took retribution from those who committed crimes, and incumbent upon Us was support of the believers.
v.c: Indeed, We sent before you ˹O Prophet˺ messengers, each to their own people, and they came to them with clear proofs. Then We inflicted punishment upon those who persisted in wickedness. For it is Our duty to help the believers.

m: He causes it to fall on
He causes it to fall on
q: It is Allaah Who sends the winds which carry the clouds, spreading them across the sky as He wills
(so that the clouds arrive at the place where Allaah intends rain to fall).
He then breaks the clouds into fragments
after which you see rain falling from its midst. When Allaah sends it
to those bondsmen whom He wills, they become happy...
v.s: It is God who sends the winds, and they stir the clouds and spread them in the sky however He wills, and He makes them fragments so you see the rain emerge from within them. And when He causes it to fall upon whom He wills of His servants, immediately they rejoice
v.c: It is Allah Who sends the winds, which then stir up ˹vapour, forming˺ clouds, which He then spreads out in the sky or piles up into masses as He wills, from which you see rain come forth. Then as soon as He causes it to fall on whoever He wills of His servants, they rejoice,

q: ...even though, before it was sent to them, they were despondent
(they had lost hope of ever receiving rain). (The falling of the rain mentioned in this verse may also refer to men's spiritual revival.)
v.s: Although they were, before it was sent down upon them - before that, in despair.
v.c: although they had utterly lost hope just before it was sent down to them.

q: of Allaah's mercy and how He revives the earth after its death. Undoubtedly,
He gives life to the dead and He has power over all things
(one should therefore never lose hope in Him).
v.s: So observe the effects of the mercy of God - how He gives life to the earth after its lifelessness. Indeed, that [same one] will give life to the dead, and He is over all things competent.
v.c: See then the impact of Allah’s mercy: how He gives life to the earth after its death! Surely That ˹same Creator˺ can raise the dead. For He is Most Capable of everything.

q: Verily, if we have to send a
they will begin to show ingratitude
(for all the bounties that Allaah had given them, not realising that Allaah's favours to them far outweighs the calamity).
v.s: But if We should send a [bad] wind and they saw [their crops] turned yellow, they would remain thereafter disbelievers.
v.c: Then if We send a ˹harsh˺ wind which they see withering ˹their˺ crops, they will definitely deny ˹old favours˺ right after.

q: (However, despite your (the Rasul's) concerted efforts, many of the Kuffaar still refuse to accept the truth because)
(the truth with the intention of accepting),
nor can you make the deaf hear a call
(indicating that they have no intention of accepting what you tell them).
v.s: So indeed, you will not make the dead hear, nor will you make the deaf hear the call when they turn their backs, retreating.
v.c: So you ˹O Prophet˺ certainly cannot make the dead hear ˹the truth˺. Nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn their backs and walk away.

q: You can make only those people hear who believe in Our Aayaat and are
v.s: And you cannot guide the blind away from their error. You will only make hear those who believe in Our verses so they are Muslims [in submission to God].
v.c: Nor can you lead the blind out of their misguidance. You can make none hear ˹the truth˺ except those who believe in Our revelations, ˹fully˺ submitting ˹to Allah˺.

q: It is Allaah Who created you in a state of weakness
then substituted strength after the weakness
and, after the strength, will again give weakness
old-age. Allaah creates whatever He wills, and He is the All Knowing, All Powerful.
v.s: God is the one who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and white hair. He creates what He wills, and He is the Knowing, the Competent.
v.c: It is Allah Who created you in a state of weakness, then developed ˹your˺ weakness into strength, then developed ˹your˺ strength into weakness and old age. He creates whatever He wills. For He is the All-Knowing, Most Capable.

q: The day when Qiyaamah will dawn, the criminals
will swear an oath saying, “We never stayed
(in the world or in the grave for)
more than a moment.” In this manner
(just as they will be deceived in not understanding the duration of their stay)
(in this world by their false hopes, by Shaytaan and by other factors which led them to kufr and sin).
v.s: And the Day the Hour appears the criminals will swear they had remained but an hour. Thus they were deluded.
v.c: And on the Day the Hour will arrive, the wicked will swear that they did not stay ˹in this world˺ more than an hour. In this way they were always deluded ˹in the world˺.

q: (many years of your life in the world)
until the Day of Resurrection. This is now that Day of Resurrection
(that it will certainly dawn on you).”
v.s: But those who were given knowledge and faith will say, "You remained the extent of God's decree until the Day of Resurrection, and this is the Day of Resurrection, but you did not used to know."
v.c: But those gifted with knowledge and faith will say ˹to them˺, “You did actually stay—as destined by Allah—until the Day of Resurrection. So here is the Day of Resurrection ˹which you denied˺! But you did not know ˹it was true˺.”

m: will be allowed to make amends
q: On this day, the excuses of the oppressors
will not benefit them, neither will they be given the opportunity
(to make amends for their wrongs by repenting or by pleasing Allaah in any other manner because this opportunity is given to men only in this world).
v.s: So that Day, their excuse will not benefit those who wronged, nor will they be asked to appease [God].
v.c: So on that Day the wrongdoers’ excuses will not benefit them, nor will they be allowed to appease ˹their Lord˺.

q: We have undoubtedly explained every type of excellent subject for people in this Qur'aan
(so that they may understand Towheed). (However, the Kuffaar are so stubborn that even)
If you bring to them an Aayah
say, “You are merely people of falsehood.”
v.s: And We have certainly presented to the people in this Qur’ān from every [kind of] example. But, [O Muhammad], if you should bring them a sign, the disbelievers will surely say, “You [believers] are but falsifiers.”
v.c: We have certainly set forth every ˹kind of˺ lesson for people in this Quran. And no matter what sign you bring to them ˹O Prophet˺, the disbelievers will definitely say ˹to the believers˺, “You are only a people of falsehood.”

q: Thus has Allaah set a seal upon the hearts of those who have no knowledge
v.s: Thus does God seal the hearts of those who do not know.
v.c: This is how Allah seals the hearts of those unwilling to know ˹the truth˺.

q: (despite the aggression and rejection of the Kuffaar).
is certainly true and do not let those who do not have conviction
v.s: So be patient. Indeed, the promise of God is truth. And let them not disquiet you who are not certain [in faith].
v.c: So be patient, for the promise of Allah certainly is true. And do not be disturbed by those who have no sure faith.
